section.p: A clean, optimized, and fully functional TWRP 12.1 recovery for Infinix Note 11 (X663), with proper dynamic partition support, data decryption, and A/B slot handling.

This custom recovery provides a complete solution for device management, including backup/restore capabilities, partition management, and custom ROM flashing with full support for modern Android partition structures.

p.strong: Unlocking the bootloader and flashing custom images may void your warranty and can brick your device if done incorrectly.

div.p: Make sure you understand all the steps and always keep a full backup of your important data before proceeding. We are not responsible for any damage to your device.

tr.td: Backup & Restore (System / Vendor / Product / Boot / Super)

section.p: Requires a working Android/TWRP build environment (Ubuntu/Debian recommended).

div.p: Create a working directory and initialize the TWRP manifest repository.

div.code:
mkdir ~/twrp-12.1-infinix-x663
cd ~/twrp-12.1-infinix-x663
repo init -u https://github.com/minimal-manifest-twrp/platform_manifest_twrp_aosp.git -b twrp-12.1
repo sync -c --no-clone-bundle --no-tags --optimized-fetch --prune --force-sync -j"$(nproc --all)"

div.p: Clone the Infinix X663 device tree from the repository.
Source the build environment setup script.
Choose the build target for the Infinix Note 11.
The resulting image will be located at:

section.div: 💡 Tip: Build time varies depending on your system resources. First-time builds take significantly longer. Ensure you have at least 150GB of free disk space.

section.p: Make sure your bootloader is unlocked and proper USB drivers are installed.

div.p: Connect your device via USB and reboot to fastboot mode.
If required by your ROM, disable verification and flash vbmeta.
Flash the compiled TWRP image to the boot partition.
Reboot your device directly into TWRP recovery.

section.h3: What You Can Do in TWRP

div.style: background-color: var(--bg-tertiary); padding: 1.5rem; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid var(--accent-green);

ul.li: Take Full Backups: Backup Boot, Super, System, Vendor, and Product partitions
Flash Custom ROMs: Install modified or alternative Android ROMs
Install Magisk: Root your device and install custom modules
Flash Kernels: Install custom kernels and optimization modules
Manage Partitions: Wipe, format, and manage device partitions
Advanced Operations: Resize partitions, mount filesystems, and more

section.div: ⚡ Important: Make sure to create a full backup of your current system before flashing anything. Always keep your important data backed up to a safe location.
